name: Echinodon
sum: A tiny heterodontosaurid known only from jaws and teeth from the earliest Cretaceous Purbeck Group of Dorset, England.
wsnote: No total length in the sources used; the skull is estimated at about 62 mm from the proportions of Heterodontosaurus, which would make it the smallest presumably adult heterodontosaurid.
holotype: Syntype series NHMUK 48209 to 48215, jaw bones with teeth from Durdlestone Bay, Isle of Purbeck, collected by Samuel Beckles and bought by the British Museum in 1876; the sources consulted also mention a lectotype.
material: Premaxilla, maxilla, lacrimal, jugal, palatine, ectopterygoid and dentary pieces with most upper and lower teeth, plus a referred dentary (NHMUK 48229) and isolated teeth from the Purbeck beds.
biology: Known only from skull bones, with an enlarged lower caniniform and a small peg-like first dentary tooth; the sources consulted do not describe its habits.
author: Owen 1861
